issues.t: Oil in spark plug wells causes misfires
issues.sym: A flashing or steady check engine light, a shaking or stumbling engine, and a burning oil smell. When the coils are pulled, the spark plug tubes are wet with oil.
issues.why: The cam (valve) cover gaskets and the spark plug tube seals harden with age and let oil run down into the plug wells. The oil soaks the ignition coils until they short out and the cylinder misfires.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read and the plug wells checked. Replace the cam cover gaskets and tube seals along with any damaged coils and plugs; just swapping coils will not last if the leak stays.

issues.t: Ignition coil failures and misfire (extended coverage)
issues.sym: Rough running, hesitation, loss of power and a check engine light with misfire codes, often on one cylinder at a time.
issues.why: The coil-on-plug ignition coils on the 3.9L V8 fail more often than they should, and on 2003 cars leaking valve cover gaskets made it worse. Ford set up an extended coverage program (07M07) for these coils and, on 2003 models, the valve cover gaskets.
issues.next: Get the misfire codes read so the failed coil can be found. The extended coverage has very likely ended by now, but a Lincoln dealer can check your VIN.

issues.t: Water in coil wells causes misfires after rain or washing
issues.sym: Misfiring, shaking and a check engine light that show up after heavy rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Water from the windshield cowl area can get past the coil covers and into the spark plug wells. Ford issued a service bulletin for 3.9L engines built through May 1, 2004 that calls for new cowl seals, coil covers and coils where needed.
issues.next: Have the plug wells checked for water and rust. Replacing the cowl seals and coil boots, and using dielectric grease on the coils, stops it from coming back.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring engine revs between gears, a transmission warning light, or the car no longer moving properly in gear.
issues.why: The five-speed automatic wears internally, and burnt or never-changed fluid and a clogged filter speed this up. Owners report failures from about 60,000 miles on.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips, have it diagnosed before it fails completely; a rebuild or replacement is usually needed at that point.

issues.t: Harsh shifts or delayed engagement into Reverse
issues.sym: A pause before the car engages Reverse, a thump when it does, or a hard shift from 2nd to 3rd gear.
issues.why: The 5R55S automatic in these years can engage Reverse late and shift harshly. Ford released bulletins covering a fluid additive, computer reprogramming and, on the 3.0L V6, a fix for a harsh 2-3 upshift.
issues.next: Ask a shop to check for stored codes and confirm the fluid is the right type and level. A computer update or fluid service often helps; mention the 5R55S bulletins to the shop.

issues.t: Front lower ball joint nuts may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the front end or steering that feels loose. In the worst case a ball joint could break.
issues.why: The nuts holding the front lower ball joints to the control arms were not tightened enough at the factory. They could loosen and let the ball joint stud crack. Ford recalled these cars to check the torque and replace ball joints if needed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 00V-359. Any clunking or loose steering should be inspected before more driving.

issues.t: Worn front lower ball joints
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, a wandering feel at highway speed, or uneven front tire wear.
issues.why: The front lower ball joints wear out, and owners report replacing them on one or both sides. On these cars the ball joint is often serviced together with the steering knuckle, which makes it a bigger job.
issues.next: Have the front end checked for play on a lift. A badly worn ball joint can separate, so do not put this off.

issues.t: Front sway bar bushings clunk
issues.sym: A popping or clunking noise from the front end over bumps and when turning at low speed.
issues.why: The original front sway bar bushings wear out on nearly every early LS. Ford redesigned the bar, bushings and brackets for 2003, and the updated parts fit the earlier cars.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm the noise source. Installing the later-style sway bar and bushings is the usual long-term fix.

issues.t: Worn tie rod ends
issues.sym: Steering that feels loose or catches when it returns to center, clunks over bumps, or tires wearing on the edges.
issues.why: Owners report the outer tie rod ends wearing loose, sometimes on both sides, especially at higher mileage.
issues.next: Have the steering linkage checked for play. Replace worn tie rod ends and get an alignment afterward.

issues.t: Wheel bearing hum or growl
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that rises with speed and may change when you steer left or right.
issues.why: Owners report front and rear wheel bearings wearing out on these heavy rear-drive sedans.
issues.next: Have a shop find which corner is noisy and replace the bearing before it gets loose.

issues.t: Overheating from a faulty thermostat
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, a check engine light comes on, and the dash may warn that engine power is being limited.
issues.why: Thermostat failures caused overheating on many early cars, mostly the V8. Ford ran a thermostat recall for some 2000 V8 cars built in a certain date range.
issues.next: Stop driving if the gauge goes into the red. Have the thermostat and cooling system checked, and ask a dealer whether any thermostat recall is open on your VIN.

issues.t: Cracked coolant tank, thermostat housing or radiator
issues.sym: Coolant puddles or a sweet smell, a low coolant warning, or the engine running hot.
issues.why: The plastic coolant expansion tank, thermostat housing and radiator tanks crack with age and heat. Owners report replacing some of these parts more than once.
issues.next: Find the leak before topping up again. Replace the cracked part and refill with the correct coolant; an overheated aluminum engine can warp a cylinder head.

issues.t: Water pump leaks or loses its impeller
issues.sym: Coolant drips near the front of the engine, a low coolant level, or the engine overheating.
issues.why: Corrosion inside the water pump can damage the impeller, so the pump stops moving coolant well, and the pump seal can start to leak. RepairPal lists overheating from a damaged impeller as a common LS problem, and owners report water pump replacements.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and coolant level. Have a pressure test done and replace the pump if it is leaking or not circulating; use the correct coolant to slow corrosion.

issues.t: Hydraulic cooling fan runs slow, overheats in traffic
issues.sym: The engine runs hot in stop-and-go traffic or at idle but cools down at highway speed.
issues.why: The LS radiator fan is driven by hydraulic fluid from the power steering system. A failing fan control actuator, pump or motor, or the wrong fluid, lets the fan spin too slowly.
issues.next: Have the fan speed and the hydraulic fan system tested. Use only the fluid Ford specifies for this system.

issues.t: Water pump hose may burst (service program)
issues.sym: A sudden coolant leak, steam from under the hood, and a rising temperature gauge, possibly at low mileage.
issues.why: Some water pump hoses were built with the wrong number of reinforcement loops and could burst. Ford ran a customer satisfaction program (04B21) to replace them.
issues.next: Ask a Lincoln dealer to check your VIN for program 04B21. Pull over and shut the engine off if you see steam or the gauge climbs.

issues.t: One side blows hot air with A/C on
issues.sym: With automatic dual-zone climate, the driver or passenger vents blow warm while the other side is cold, or the heat won't shut off on one side.
issues.why: The dual coolant control valve that meters hot coolant to each side of the heater sticks or fails. A faulty climate control unit or low refrigerant can cause the same symptom. Ford covered this in TSB 03-03-04.
issues.next: Have the refrigerant charge checked first, then the dual coolant control valve. The valve is usually the fix.

issues.t: A/C refrigerant leak or compressor failure
issues.sym: The A/C slowly gets weaker and then blows warm, or the compressor clutch slips or stops engaging.
issues.why: Refrigerant leaks and failed compressors or clutches are common complaints as these cars age.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested before recharging it. A recharge alone will not last if there is a leak.

issues.t: Power window regulator breaks
issues.sym: A window that grinds or crunches, drops into the door, goes up crooked or stops moving. Rear windows are the most common.
issues.why: The window regulators wear out and break. Ford issued a bulletin (04-6-3) for rear windows on cars built through January 2002, and owners report regulator failures at all four doors.
issues.next: Replace the regulator (and the motor if it is worn). Tape or prop up a dropped window to keep rain out until it is fixed.

issues.t: Door handle cracks or breaks
issues.sym: An inside or outside door handle that snaps, feels loose, or no longer opens the door; the driver door is the usual one.
issues.why: The plastic handles and latch linkage crack with age, and owners report the driver door handle failing more than once.
issues.next: Replace the broken handle or latch part. If a door will not open from inside, fix it soon for safety.

issues.t: Moisture inside headlamps
issues.sym: Fog or water droplets inside a headlight, dim light output, or bulbs burning out early.
issues.why: The headlamp seals let moisture in. Ford's bulletin (03-16-02) calls for resealing the lamp, or replacing it if water has pooled or stained it.
issues.next: Have the lamp resealed if it is only fogged. Replace it if water is pooling inside.

issues.t: 17-inch chrome wheels can crack at lug holes (recall)
issues.sym: Noise or vibration from a wheel, or lug nuts that keep loosening.
issues.why: Some 17-inch chrome wheels were not heat-treated and could crack around the lug nut holes. If driving continued, a wheel could come off. Ford recalled these cars to inspect and replace wheels.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 03V-136. Stop driving if a wheel makes noise or the lug nuts are loose.

issues.t: Fuel tank can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell or drips under the rear of the car, and sometimes a check engine light.
issues.why: Some fuel tanks had a thin wall section in the lower half that could crack and leak, creating a fire risk. Ford recalled these cars to replace the tank.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 05V-113. Do not park in a garage or keep driving with a fuel smell; have it inspected right away.

issues.t: Cracked PCV hose causes rough idle or stalling (service program)
issues.sym: Rough or surging idle, stalling, a whistling sound, or a check engine light with lean codes.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) hose on the 3.0L V6 cracks and lets unmetered air into the engine. Ford ran a service campaign (08-N-01) to replace the hose on 2003-2005 LS V6 cars.
issues.next: Ask a Lincoln dealer whether campaign 08-N-01 was done on your VIN. If not, a new PCV hose is a simple fix.

issues.t: Electronic throttle fault and reduced power
issues.sym: A throttle control warning light, check engine light, a high or rolling idle, or the engine going into a limited-power mode.
issues.why: The electronic throttle body and its sensors can fault, and sludge in the throttle body can upset airflow. Ford issued several bulletins for throttle control codes such as P2106 and P2135 on these years.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Cleaning or replacing the throttle body, or a computer update, is the usual fix.

issues.t: Electric parking brake fault message
issues.sym: A 'service park brake' message or parking brake warning, or a parking brake that will not set or release.
issues.why: Starting in 2003 the LS uses an electric parking brake. Its module and actuator can fault, and Ford released bulletins for park brake warning codes.
issues.next: Use Park and chock the wheels on hills until it is fixed. Have the parking brake module and actuator diagnosed with a scan tool.

issues.t: ABS and traction control lights from wheel speed sensor faults
issues.sym: The ABS and traction control lights come on, often while driving, and anti-lock braking is turned off.
issues.why: Wheel speed sensor circuit faults (codes like C1145 and C1155) set these lights. Ford issued a bulletin on it.
issues.next: Normal braking still works, but have the codes read and the faulty sensor or wiring repaired so ABS works again.

issues.t: Airbag light on from failed clockspring
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on or flashes, and the horn or steering wheel buttons may stop working.
issues.why: The clockspring, a coiled ribbon cable in the steering column that connects the driver airbag and wheel controls, wears and breaks.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read. The driver airbag may not work while the light is on, so get the clockspring replaced.

issues.t: Alternator stops charging
issues.sym: A battery or charging warning, dim lights, a dead battery, or the car running poorly as voltage drops.
issues.why: Owners report alternator failures, sometimes leading to a flashing check engine light or limp mode.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested before buying a new battery. Replace the alternator if it fails the test.

issues.t: Fuel pump failure or hard hot starts
issues.sym: Long cranking before the engine starts, especially when warm, stalling, or a car that cranks but will not start.
issues.why: Owners report in-tank fuel pump failures, sometimes more than once. Leaking fuel injectors can also cause hard starting when hot.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested while the problem is happening before replacing parts.

issues.t: Catalytic converter fouled or failed
issues.sym: A check engine light with catalyst efficiency or oxygen sensor codes, a failed emissions test, or loss of power.
issues.why: Oil from leaking valve covers and long periods of misfiring can foul an oxygen sensor and plug a catalytic converter.
issues.next: Fix any oil leak or misfire first, then have the converter and sensors tested. Replacing a converter without fixing the cause will just ruin the new one.
